title.narrative: Nicaragua Hurricanes Eta and Iota Emergency Response project

description.narrative:
UNOPS supports Nicaragua’s emergency response and recovery needs after the devastation caused by hurricanes Eta and Iota. The Nicaragua Hurricanes Eta and Iota Emergency Response project helps the country’s disaster-relief response and restoration of services and economic activities in critical sectors in the most affected communities.

The project prioritizes the country’s efforts in the Caribbean Coast Autonomous Regions which were impacted by the compound effects of the two hurricanes. The Autonomous Regions have the highest incidence of extreme poverty in the country, making their population—which includes a large number of indigenous people and Afro-descendants—especially vulnerable to external shocks. The project will also finance the rehabilitation and resilient reconstruction of prioritized public and community infrastructure and housing.

The hurricanes compounded the economic and health challenges of the COVID-19 Pandemic. As such, there is a need to continue to provide the affected population with timely emergency relief, as well as help them rebuild their communities in a resilient manner.

The project will also focus on restoring the income of affected populations in critical economic activities, with a focus on the small-scale fisheries sector. Affected communities and their representatives will be involved in prioritizing project activities and ensuring that activities are tailored to their needs and cultural preferences.

The $80 million credit for the Nicaragua Hurricanes Eta and Iota Emergency Response Project is financed by the International Development Agency (IDA), the World Bank’s fund for the poorest countries, and will be implemented in collaboration with the United Nations Office of Project Services (UNOPS).
